query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for structural use under extreme-temperature conditions, what single intervention could improve high-temperature oxygen resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the temperature, atmosphere, and exposure conditions under which it should work, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding Cr to refractory high-entropy alloys to form a CrTaO4-based oxide layer will improve high-temperature oxygen resistance.
generation.intervention: adding 5-10 at.% Cr to the alloy composition
generation.conditions: exposure to 1000°C in an oxidizing atmosphere (air) for 100 hours
generation.structural_mediator: formation of a CrTaO4-based oxide layer
generation.mechanism: the CrTaO4-based oxide layer acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion, reducing oxidation and degradation of the alloy
generation.predicted_outcome: a 30% reduction in oxidation rate relative to the untreated alloy
generation.uncertainty: the actual improvement in oxygen resistance may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: compare the oxidation rates of untreated and Cr-modified refractory high-entropy alloys in a thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) experiment
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the oxidation rate of the Cr-modified alloy is not at least 20% lower than that of the untreated alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
